clue.text: Stage actor takes instruction from me?

definitions.meaning: a stagecoach, a horse-drawn vehicle running between stages, is also known by this shorter name
a drama tutor or trainer is the person an actor takes direction from

explanation.surface: A theatre voice asks whether the performer on stage is following its directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' reads as the theatre, but it is the stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a stagecoach, and a trainer or tutor who instructs a performer.

clue.text: Detective about to have a thug — hardened criminal ——- apprehended thus?

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: D is short for detective, as in DI or DS

explanation.surface: A detective is about to collar a hardened thug, arresting him in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun after 'hardened', but is the anagram signal for D, C, A THUG and HARDENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Seized in the very act of the crime is how such an arrest happens.

clue.text: Plant boss needing capital

indicators.note: needing means lacking, so the capital or first letter is missing

parts.note: a master is a boss

explanation.surface: A factory manager needs investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' reads as money but means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower of the daisy family, such as the Michaelmas daisy.

clue.text: Fellow would have hold over party

indicators.note: to have means to hold within, so one piece is put inside

parts.note: he'd is short for he would
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
to own is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: A man is expected to take charge of a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively country-dance gathering, a kind of social event.

clue.text: Key player given freedom to move

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby, such as a full-back
space is room to move freely

explanation.surface: A footballer is given room to run with the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard key that deletes the character before the cursor bears this name.

clue.text: I'll get absorbed in first half of book — good example of non-fiction

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside the other piece
picks the first two of the four letters

parts.note: I'll is I will, giving the letter I

explanation.surface: A reader will get lost in a fine work of non-fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography, the true life story of a person, is a common type of factual book.

clue.text: Dodgy character from Prague reportedly investigated

indicators.note: reportedly means as is said, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tout, a dodgy ticket seller, who is Czech

explanation.surface: A shady man from the Czech capital has been looked into.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something out is to examine or look into it.

clue.text: Spy film not successful at first

definitions.meaning: a secret agent planted to lie dormant until called on
a film that only becomes a hit some time after release

explanation.surface: A spy movie flopped on release.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dormant planted agent and a slow-burning surprise hit share this name.

clue.text: Careful to keep wine in case, unopened

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so one piece goes inside
without its opening, the first letter is removed

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case
tent is a Spanish red wine used for communion

explanation.surface: Someone is careful to store wine in a crate that stays sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as a crate but is a grammatical case: DATIVE, unopened, gives ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heedful and watchful means paying close attention.

clue.text: Writer producing fliers Chinese style?

parts.note: ernes are sea eagles, a crossword favourite
the manner of the Ming dynasty of China

explanation.surface: An author produces Chinese-style kites.
explanation.walkthrough: The query marks a phrase as fanciful: 'the Ming way' for Chinese style.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Unstable hut people abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A shaky shack has been deserted by its occupants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' seems to describe the hut, but signals the anagram of HUT PEOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang idiom means crazy, mentally unbalanced or in a mess.

clue.text: Scoffed as one school is mentioned …

indicators.note: being mentioned means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked because a particular school came up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked, but means gobbled. ETON is the elite English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to wolf it down, so scoffed means consumed greedily.

clue.text: … and another that takes mostly tough line

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: hard means tough
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A second school is described as taking a fairly hard line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' follows on from the previous clue: a second school. HARROW is the English public school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Like Eton in the clue before, this is a famous English boarding school, hence 'another'.

clue.text: Worker wearing captain's clothes

indicators.note: the piece being worn sits inside the clothing piece, so one is placed within the other

parts.note: skip is a short name for a captain, as of a curling or bowls team; with the possessive, skip's
an ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee has put on the team captain's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers made for the slopes are winter sports clothing.

clue.text: Cabinet admits Labour unlikely to remain dispirited?

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a console is a cabinet for a radio or television
Lab is short for the Labour party

explanation.surface: The government's cabinet concedes that Labour is unlikely to stay downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' and 'Labour' paint politics; the cabinet is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can be comforted will not stay downhearted for long.

clue.text: Lawbreaker initially breaking into house through back door

indicators.note: one piece passes through the other, so it sits inside it
back means the word door is read from the end to the start

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned around

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of breaking

parts.note: into gives in

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks into a house through the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOOR into ROOD; B from 'initially breaking', IN and HO go through it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: Uncivilised watering holes, popular around Aussie capital

parts.note: bars are watering holes, two of them here

indicators.note: around means the popular piece encloses the letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: capital means the first letter

explanation.surface: Australian pubs are described as rough places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie capital' suggests Canberra but is just the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it means primitive and lacking culture.

clue.text: BBC chief's floral tribute for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: a wreath is a ring of flowers laid in tribute

explanation.surface: The head of the BBC's flowers are meant for the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith founded the British Broadcasting Corporation and was its first Director-General.

clue.text: From Renaissance artist rude works meeting resistance

indicators.note: works as a verb means is worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Crude pieces from a Renaissance painter face opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for paintings, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the German painter and engraver of the Northern Renaissance.

clue.text: Ribbon is right on head of old dog, not tail

indicators.note: on the head means placed at the very front of the following pieces
the clue insists the right letter sits at the front, not where it ends the run, so it is shifted from end to start

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A rosette is pinned on an old dog at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD DOG gives O + SETTER; its last letter R ('right') goes to the head, 'not tail', making ROSETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon gathered into a circular badge, awarded at shows.

clue.text: In spring, take run in the morning and dip

indicators.note: in the spring means the run piece goes inside the spring piece

parts.note: a source is a spring where a river rises
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A jogger goes for a morning run in springtime and then a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' reads as the season but is a water source; 'dip' reads as a swim but is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a thick sauce for scooping with crisps, and soured cream is a common one.

clue.text: Photograph couples in unconventional pose

indicators.note: posed unconventionally means set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Pairs are snapped in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a picture taken at very short range.

clue.text: Notice a chap's imbibing second drink

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a chap is a male; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An advert shows a man drinking a second glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of chap's is 'is'. ADAM'S ALE is a jocular name for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is jokingly called the first man's ale, being all he had to drink in Eden.

clue.text: Sweetie making heads turn

indicators.note: turn means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nob is slang for head, so two heads are nob and nob

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is so attractive that people look round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetie' reads as a darling but is a sweet; 'heads turn' looks like admiring glances.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sweet or chocolate confection; sweetie is a British word for a sweet.

clue.text: Nonsense put about by, for instance, Lloyd George?

indicators.note: put about means turned around, as a ship is, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for instance
David Lloyd George was a Liberal prime minister, so he is a Lib

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Welsh statesman spread rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' reads as spread, but is the turnaround signal; Lloyd George was a Liberal prime minister, so a Lib.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for rubbish or worthless talk.

clue.text: Intermittent fondness for poetry

indicators.note: intermittent means stopping and starting, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone has an on-off liking for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so collectively they are poetry.

clue.text: Meaning to wander from place to place

definitions.meaning: the gist or general sense of what someone says

definitions.text: to wander from place to place
definitions.meaning: to move aimlessly, carried along without purpose

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the gist of an argument; the verb is to roam aimlessly.

clue.text: Mate fled below at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's mate ran below deck during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a ship's officer in this nautical picture, but is a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is a partner or close associate, as a mate is.

clue.text: Dope stuck in sandhills near southern headland

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: dunes are hills of sand
gen and dope are both slang for information

explanation.surface: A drug stash is buried in the dunes by a headland in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' reads as drugs but means information. Dungeness is a shingle headland in Kent, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This promontory on the Kent coast is a cape jutting into the English Channel.

clue.text: Goodness! Pastry concoction's terribly short of filling

parts.note: a pie is a concoction of pastry; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: without its filling means only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a pie is terribly underfilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' reads as an exclamation but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, a form of virtue or moral goodness.
